Using this book

A worked line has a complete sequence to the point where the video stops. A brief mention stops at its actual branching position. The displayed end positions are starting points for discussion, not claims of a forced win.

Source: jacksark, I Studied the Sicilian Defense So You Don't Have To, and the creator's linked Lichess study. The McDonnell discussion ends at 21:04; the next opening is Mengarini. The description's chapter times differ, so the lesson uses the spoken section boundary, also checked on the video board.

Move checks and source corrections

Every move was checked for legality. The creator's PGN resolves several automatic-caption errors. Teaching explanations here were written for Misika; the video's numerical evaluations and game percentages are not used as engine results.

  • The Ne1 attack uses 13.Qf3, verified on the video board at 04:52 and in the linked study.
  • The en passant capture is ...cxd3, removing the pawn on d4.
  • The queen exchange uses Nxc6 and ...bxc6.
  • The ...Nd4 fork threatens c2, not c7.
  • After the early Bb5+ and Nc3, the central capture is ...dxe4.

Two extra queenless sidelines in the study were omitted because they are not discussed in this video segment. The queen-trap line stops at ...c2, the video's narrated endpoint.
